title: Deploying Terraform to Azure using GitHub Actions (OIDC)
excerpt: Run Terraform init, plan and apply in GitHub Actions using Azure OIDC authentication

body.raw:
<BlogImage 
  src="/terraformazure.png" 
  alt="Terraform & GitHub Actions"
  size="large" 
/>

---

## What This Guide Covers

This article assumes that Backend storage exists for storing state

Use **ONE** of the terraform backend options:

<Prerequisites
  articles={[
    {
      title: "Manual Terraform Backend Setup in Azure",
      href: "/blog/backendportal",
      description: "Create the Azure Storage Account manually via the Azure Portal."
    },
    {
      title: "Terraform Backend Bootstrap using Azure OIDC",
      href: "/blog/backendtf",
      description: "Provision the backend using GitHub Actions and federated identity."
    }
  ]}
/>

It also assumes:

- OIDC authentication between GitHub and Azure is configured
- Required repository secrets are stored

If not, complete the backend and identity setup first.

This guide focuses purely on:

→ Running Terraform from GitHub Actions  
→ Using OIDC authentication  
→ Connecting to a remote Azure backend  

---

# Deployment Architecture

GitHub Actions  
→ OIDC Authentication  
→ Azure  
→ Remote Backend (Storage Account)  
→ Infrastructure Deployment  

No local execution required.  
No stored credentials.

---

# Minimal Terraform Configuration

Below is a simple Terraform setup using the AzureRM provider and OIDC authentication.

## main.tf

```hcl:title=main.tf
terraform {
  required_providers {
    azurerm = {
      source = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = "~> 4.61.0"
    }
  }
backend "azurerm" {}
}


provider "azurerm" {
   features {}
   use_oidc = true
}

# Resource Group
resource "azurerm_resource_group" "rg" {
  name     = local.rg_name
  location = var.location
}
```
## variables.tf
```hcl:title=variables.tf
variable "location" {
  type    = string
  default = "westeurope"
}
```

## locals.tf
```hcl:title=locals.tf
locals {
  base    = "simpletst"
  rg_name = "${local.base}-rg"
}
```

This keeps the infrastructure example intentionally simple.

# GitHub Actions Workflow

This workflow:
- Authenticates using OIDC
- Initializes Terraform with remote backend
- Validates and formats code
- Runs plan
- Applies automatically on main

## terraform.yaml
```yaml:title=terraform.yaml
name: Terraform Plan & Apply

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - ".github/Terraform/**"
      - ".github/workflows/terraform.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

env:
  ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
  ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
  ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}

  RESOURCE_GROUP: <backend-resource-group>
  STORAGE_ACCOUNT: <backend-storage-account>
  location: westeurope

jobs:
  terraform:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: .github/Terraform
        shell: bash

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1

      - name: Terraform Init
        run: |
          terraform init \
            -backend-config="resource_group_name=$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            -backend-config="storage_account_name=$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
            -backend-config="container_name=tfstate" \
            -backend-config="key=terraform.tfstate" \
            -backend-config="use_oidc=true"

      - name: Terraform Format
        run: terraform fmt -recursive

      - name: Terraform Validate
        run: terraform validate

      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan -input=false -var location=$location

      - name: Terraform Apply
        run: terraform apply -auto-approve -input=false -var location=$location
```

## How It Works

1. GitHub requests an OIDC token
2. Azure validates it via federated identity
3. Terraform initializes using the remote backend
4. Plan and apply execute inside the runner
5. State is written to Azure Storage

### This ensures:

- No local state
- No client secrets
- Reproducible deployments
- Fully automated infrastructure changes

# Deployment Flow

Push to main

→ GitHub workflow triggers

→ Terraform runs

→ Azure resources update

→ Remote state updated

Infrastructure becomes Git-driven.


# Result

You now have:

- Remote Terraform state
- OIDC-based authentication
- CI/CD infrastructure deployment
- Zero local dependency

This completes the GitOps-style workflow.

# Sources used

- [How to Use Terraform in GitHub Actions](https://www.env0.com/blog/terraform-github-actions)
- [Deploy to Azure infrastructure with GitHub Actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/devops/deliver/iac-github-actions)

`,(0,t.jsxDEV)(e.pre,{children:(0,t.jsxDEV)(e.code,{className:"language-yaml:title=terraform.yaml",children:`name: Terraform Plan & Apply\r
\r
on:\r
  push:\r
    branches:\r
      - main\r
    paths:\r
      - ".github/Terraform/**"\r
      - ".github/workflows/terraform.yaml"\r
  workflow_dispatch:\r
\r
permissions:\r
  id-token: write\r
  contents: read\r
\r
env:\r
  ARM_CLIENT_ID: \${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}\r
  ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: \${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}\r
  ARM_TENANT_ID: \${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}\r
\r
  RESOURCE_GROUP: <backend-resource-group>\r
  STORAGE_ACCOUNT: <backend-storage-account>\r
  location: westeurope\r
\r
jobs:\r
  terraform:\r
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\r
\r
    defaults:\r
      run:\r
        working-directory: .github/Terraform\r
        shell: bash\r
\r
    steps:\r
      - name: Checkout\r
        uses: actions/checkout@v3\r
\r
      - name: Setup Terraform\r
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1\r
\r
      - name: Terraform Init\r
        run: |\r
          terraform init \\\r
            -backend-config="resource_group_name=$RESOURCE_GROUP" \\\r
            -backend-config="storage_account_name=$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \\\r
            -backend-config="container_name=tfstate" \\\r
            -backend-config="key=terraform.tfstate" \\\r
            -backend-config="use_oidc=true"\r
\r
      - name: Terraform Format\r
        run: terraform fmt -recursive\r
\r
      - name: Terraform Validate\r
        run: terraform validate\r
\r
      - name: Terraform Plan\r
        run: terraform plan -input=false -var location=$location\r
\r
      - name: Terraform Apply\r
        run: terraform apply -auto-approve -input=false -var location=$location
